near_miss.lead: Rus. zelenyj lug 'green meadow' ~ ON gull ... i lyngvi liggr
near_miss.why_not: Fafnismal has gold lying in the heather, with no 'green' and no meadow; the Russian is the everyday epic 'green meadow' (horses put out to graze). Only link is the doubtful lug ~ lyng equation. Nothing phrasal.

near_miss.lead: Rus. na zelenom lugu ... vo krugu ~ ON hringi grǿnna lyngva
near_miss.why_not: The look-alike is surface only: zelenyj and grǿnn are not cognate; the Russian is a round dance on a meadow, the skaldic line a kenning tied to Fafnir's gold. The contexts do not match.

near_miss.lead: Rus. na chetvertom godu ~ Latv. ceturtajā gadā 'in the fourth year'
near_miss.why_not: Same branch (Balto-Slavic), and a generic time expression.

near_miss.lead: Rus. ni otec ni mati ni rodna rodina ~ Latv. mātes radi
near_miss.why_not: Same branch; listing kin is generic.
Rus. kopyto is not cognate with śapha (see error line). The contexts (a hoof-print on the steppe vs. a ritual goat stepping) do not match.

near_miss.lead: various root co-occurrences (new/dark, mother/sleep, live/house, father-mother, wolf, sleep-lie, sharp nose, sea, new, brother-sister, rib, eyes)
near_miss.why_not: Read closely: these share only everyday vocabulary, with no shared collocation or figure in a congruent context. Several 'wolf' hits are the personal name Vuk (see errors).

near_miss.lead: *dʰuh₂mós + *welH- 'roll': Rus. dym (stolbom) valit ~ Lat. uoluit ... fumum
near_miss.why_not: Both words are cognate, but the syntax differs: Russian valit is intransitive with smoke as subject, while Lucretius has Aetna rolling smoke as object. The Russian is an everyday idiom ('smoke billows') in 18th- and 19th-c. soldier songs. Search finds the pair only in Russian and Latin, plus a Homeric-hymn ἑλίσσετο hit that is not about smoke. 'Rolling smoke' is too natural an image to claim as inherited.

near_miss.lead: *kr̥snó- + *gʷriHwéh₂-: Rus. cherna griva (of a horse) ~ Skt kṛṣṇagrīva
near_miss.why_not: Both words are cognate. MBh 7.22.42 uses kṛṣṇagrīvāḥ of horses (found by search). But the Russian formula is about falling onto the horse's mane, and Skt grīvā means 'neck' (a coat colouring), not 'mane'. A basic colour term plus a body part is too generic, and there are only two branches with no third.

near_miss.lead: star falls from the sky: Rus. zvezda s nebes upadala ~ Latv. zvaigzne debesīs iekrita
near_miss.why_not: Same branch (Balto-Slavic); the verb is renewed and the image generic.

near_miss.lead: *médʰu + *gʰóstis: Rus. pivom-medom ugostila ~ ON miði ... gefa gestum
near_miss.why_not: The ON is translated prose (a cupbearer story). Rus. ugostit' is a denominative verb, not a phrase, and serving mead to guests is generic hospitality.

near_miss.lead: Rus. med sladkij ~ Latv. medutiņa saldumiņš
near_miss.why_not: The slab partner is the same branch. The wider *swéh₂du- médʰu formula is reported as a search lead, not a claim.

near_miss.lead: tongue and teeth: derzhi jazyk za zubami ~ jambha ... jihvā
near_miss.why_not: A Russian proverb versus an AV healing charm. The tongue and teeth are named in different functions; no shared figure.
Rus. podymites' means 'rise' (podymat'sja), not 'smoke' (mapping error). Wild winds alone are generic.

near_miss.lead: Rus. solnca novago luchami ~ Lat. solis noua ... lumina
near_miss.why_not: All three words are cognate, but the Russian is a learned panegyric ode-song (Moscow lit by the new sun), so not traditional diction. Lucretius is physics (the sun's light born anew). A coincidence.

near_miss.lead: waters as sisters: Volga 'sister' of Lake Il'men' ~ dvayī́bhiḥ svásr̥bhiḥ
near_miss.why_not: In RV 9.72.3 the 'sisters' are the fingers pressing soma, not rivers, so the contexts do not match.

near_miss.lead: weapons gleam like or in the sun: blestit ~ blika ... sólin skínn
near_miss.why_not: The verbs are only distantly related (*bʰley- extensions); a simile versus a description; a generic image.

near_miss.lead: grief as drying or cooking: sushit ... pechal' ~ śuṣka ... pacyamāna
near_miss.why_not: The MBh line is about food (cooked, dry), not grief. Rus. pechal' < *pekʷ- (cf. Gk κήδεα πέσσει, recalled) is lexical, not phrasal, and the slab has no congruent partner.

near_miss.lead: potupil ochi vo syru zemlju ~ χθόνα τύπτε μετώπῳ
near_miss.why_not: Casting the eyes down (sadness) is not striking the ground with the forehead (dying). Potupit' is not plausibly from *stewp-.

search_lead.cognate: *médʰu (мёд, μέθυ, medu, mádhu) + *swéh₂du- (ἡδύς, swēte, svādú); the Russian сладкий (Balto-Slavic *sald-, cf. Latv. salds) renews the adjective
search_lead.argument: Noun + epithet: 'sweet mead/honey-drink' in feasting and hall-drinking contexts. Homer has the formulaic line-end κρέα τ' ἄσπετα καὶ μέθυ ἡδύ. Finnsburh 39 has swētne medo as the drink of the hall paid back in battle. Vedic has svādú with mádhu of soma or food. The byliny's тур рог меду сладкого is the drink served to the hero at a feast or challenge. Weaknesses: honey is naturally sweet, the Slavic adjective is renewed, and the byliny are late.

error.evidence: A satem reflex of *ḱ would be s-, not k-; so it is not cognate with Skt śapha.

error.evidence: The repeated 'X ciϑra apa duuarata' with apa is a verb of motion, not the noun 'door'.
